paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's people get everything they need from God Himself, so they never have to go shopping anywhere else. The Levites had no portion or inheritance with Israel, and Moses says "the LORD is their inheritance" (Deuteronomy 18:2). No tribal land, and they were still covered, because the One who chose them was providing for them (Deuteronomy 18:5). So when you feel like you're running short, remember who your supply comes from.

That's why the nations' ways were off limits. Moses says Israel must not imitate them, and he names things like divination, casting spells and inquiring of the dead (Deuteronomy 18:9-11). Moses ends it with one line: "You must be blameless before the LORD your God" (Deuteronomy 18:13). If God is your inheritance, you don't need a shady back door to find out what's coming. You can bring your questions to Him.

And here's the good part: God didn't leave them guessing. He promised a prophet like Moses, and the LORD says, "I will put My words in his mouth" (Deuteronomy 18:18). The people had been afraid of God's voice at Horeb, and the LORD said "They have spoken well" (Deuteronomy 18:17). So listen to what God has actually said, and weigh every voice against it, because a message that does not come true is not from Him (Deuteronomy 18:22). That's why I keep my ovens ready, friend, and this one isn't over, because Moses is nowhere near done preaching.
